phase0.containerReprovisionedNote: This container is not the one Stage 3C-R measured. The Soup checkout, the venv and the FORGE_DATASET_V2 exports survived; the pipeline was re-executed rather than assumed, and the LoRA adapter came back bit-identical to Stage 3C-R's.

parents.note: Both parent certifications are read and neither is written. Their BLOCKED results stand.

inventory.searchDiscipline: Only the caches, stores and project folders where a model legitimately lives. No recursive scan of unrelated personal directories was performed.
inventory.exclusionRule: A model this project generated is not a model this project acquired.

ollama.reconstructionNote: No Ollama installation and no GGUF artifact exists on this machine, so the inference-only-versus-trainable distinction had nothing to apply to. Had one existed, a lossy reverse conversion to force training is forbidden by the brief and would not have been attempted.

fixtureRejection.why: The Stage 3C-R pipeline harness is HF-format and technically trainable, and it is still not a base model: it is randomly initialised with no publisher, no license and no version. The gate rejects it on provenance, which is the outcome that proves the gate does something.

gitLane.note: Anonymous git read works. Git LFS objects are NOT served on this lane, so a repository that stores weights in LFS yields pointer stubs, not weights.
gitLane.lfsNote: Git LFS objects are not served on the anonymous lane, so any repository storing weights in LFS yields pointer stubs. That rules out the usual way a model reaches GitHub.

githubHttpLane.consequence: GitHub release assets are not an available channel: the git lane is served and the HTTP download lane is not.

pypi.note: The full PyPI simple index was retrieved and searched. Every Qwen-named package is a third-party wrapper or client; no package distributes provenance-established trainable causal-LM weights.

objectStores.gcs: AUTHORIZED as an object store; no authorized model bucket is declared anywhere in this project.
objectStores.s3: AUTHORIZED as an object store; an AWS config file exists on this machine but declares no model bucket, and no credentials were inspected or used.

acquisitionAttempts.egressPolicyBypassedNote: huggingface.co and its CDN remain denied. No proxy bypass, URL rewriting, undocumented proxy, unauthorized mirror or third-party archive was used. An HF-owned alternate endpoint would have been the same evasion wearing a different hostname, and was not used either.

squattedBucket.rule: A BUCKET, REPOSITORY OR DIRECTORY NAME IS NEVER EVIDENCE OF WHAT IS INSIDE IT
squattedBucket.observed: gs://gpt-2, the bucket OpenAI's own download_model.py once used, is reachable and now holds a single unrelated HTML file uploaded by a third party in 2026.
squattedBucket.consequence: Matching on the bucket name would have pulled an attacker-controlled object into a training pipeline under the label "GPT-2, official".
squattedBucket.enforcement: Provenance is established from the artifact's own content, hashes and license, and from a publisher that can be named — never from where it happens to sit.

measured.historicalUse: the bucket openai/gpt-2's download_model.py once fetched from

squattedBucket.actedOnNote: Nothing was downloaded from it. It is recorded because the near miss is the finding.

suppliedModel.discipline: The declared path is the only place this looks. There is no fallback search: a stage that hunts for something model-shaped when the declared path is wrong will eventually train on the wrong thing and report it as the right one.
suppliedModel.declaredFieldsNote: Path-derived hashes are computed from the files. Identity, version, source, license, parameter count and aggregate hash must be declared by whoever supplies the model; inferring them from a directory is the failure this envelope exists to prevent.

trainability.ranAgainstBaseModelNote: Phase 8 loads the accepted base model through Soup. No model was accepted, so it did not run.

harnessSelfTest.purpose: Exercises the same code path end to end so the contract ships tested rather than merely written.

compute.extrapolationRefused: The harness throughput is a fact about a 1.07M-parameter random model, not a prediction about a 0.5B one. Reporting it as the campaign's feasibility would be exactly the parameter-count estimate the brief forbids, run backwards.

harnessSelfTest.note: Throughput is measured per run and is not part of the certification body: a wall-clock number would make the hash depend on how busy the machine was.

requirements.why: a candidate whose parent cannot be identified cannot be reproduced
source and license are decided before training, not after
the task is text-shaped and needs one
the pinned engine has to be able to load it
a gradient must have been observed, not assumed
a run that cannot finish is not a run

campaign.startedNote: The activation gate did not open. The campaign is not redesigned, not partially run and not approximated.

selectorLimitation.misreadingToAvoid: This is NOT deterministic Nexus's relational accuracy. Nexus emits graph-level signals and no action at all; NEXUS_RELATIONAL_SELECTOR_V1 is one policy built on those signals, and its score is that policy's score. A different policy over the same signals could do better or worse without Nexus having changed.
selectorLimitation.rawSignalsPreservedWhy: Future hybrid work needs the signals themselves, not one policy's collapse of them into a choice.

interpretation: Stage 3C-R.1 is BLOCKED on acquisition, not on infrastructure. The pipeline was re-executed in a freshly reprovisioned container and every step passed, reproducing Stage 3C-R's LoRA adapter bit-for-bit (21550fad0b01099b…). What does not exist is a base model: every model host remains denied or unreachable, and of the channels that ARE open — PyPI, anonymous GitHub git, GCS, S3, GitLab — none carries a causal LM whose publisher, license and version can be named. The one HF-format artifact on this machine is this project's own randomly-initialised harness, which the gate rejects on provenance. The nearest miss was gs://gpt-2, OpenAI's historical bucket, which is reachable and now holds an unrelated file uploaded by a third party; matching on the bucket name would have put an attacker-controlled object into a training run.
